title: Ordinary canonical integral purity and completed trace transpose
statement: Fix the finite-field and coefficient setting $P$ of [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and finite coefficient subfields of a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and fix $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$, $p:Z\to Y$ with $j$ open, $p$ proper, and $f=p\circ j$ a $k$-morphism smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the actual complete finite-Tor integral categories, completed pullback and tensor, and the specified compact-support/exceptional adjunctions of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Fix the full coefficient system $S$, models $M$, a finite field $E$, an integral model $m$, and a Stage $A$ of [def-pur-tower-trace-comparison-data]. Suppose $a^T_E$ is invertible and has the prescribed finite reductions. For every common finite-Tor $K$, the underlying morphism of RationalSmoothPurityCanonical.integralMap is adicTranspose of the explicit completed inverse-projection word formed with counitTrace$(a^T_E)$, the Stage tensor and open models, and the normalized unit isomorphism. This compares the ordinary and completed integral tensor coordinates; no rational localization or common-stage assertion is made.

proof.text: Transport the Stage unit orientation through the ordinary Tate and unit identifications. Its finite reductions and finiteIntegration_smoothPurityMap show its trace is normalized. Apply integralMap_eq_adicTraceTranspose to use this orientation. The augmentation comparison between ordinary and completed tensor is invertible on these finite-Tor inputs. Its projection square sends inverse ordinary projection to inverse completed projection. IsUnitNormalized identifies right unitors and IsJNormalized identifies the tensor-source coordinates on the same K-flat representatives. Thus the compact-support words agree. Apply the specified adjunction homEquiv and take underlying arrows.

theorem canonical_integral_transpose [QuasiCompact (j ≫ p)]
    [IsSeparated (j ≫ p)] [LocallyOfFiniteType (j ≫ p)]
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (P.coefficients.l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (P.coefficients.l : Y.residueField y)]
    (S : ConstructibleExceptionalCoefficients.System P.coefficients.l P.coefficients.Qbar
      P.field P.coefficients.different (f := j ≫ p))
    (M : FieldShriekSystem.Models P) (E : FieldShriekSystem.Index P)
    (m : FieldExtensionTowers.IntegralModel P M E j p d)
    (A : Stage P j p d S.ring M E m)
    (hA : PrescribedUnitReductions P j p d S.ring M E m A
      (orientation P j p d S.ring M E m A))
    [IsIso (orientation P j p d S.ring M E m A)]
    (K : finiteTorConstructibleIntegralCategory P.coefficients.l E.val Y) :
    (RationalSmoothPurityCanonical.integralMap (atField P E) (j ≫ p)
      (SpTowerGamma.factorization j p) S d K).hom =
      adicTranspose P.field P.coefficients E.val (j ≫ p) S.ring
        (SpTowerGamma.factorization j p) ⟨_, A.tensorTor K⟩ K
        (adicTraceMap P.coefficients.l E.val A.models A.openComparison
          (SpTowerGamma.factorization j p)
          (PurUnitTrace.tateUnit P.field P.coefficients E.val d X) K.obj
          (A.completionIso K) (A.projectionIso K)
          (counitTrace P j p d S.ring M E m A
            (orientation P j p d S.ring M E m A) ≫ A.unitIso.hom))
